correctness.rationale: The inverse Lagrange columns have reciprocal-chord denominators P_j and numerator coefficient norm between 1 and sqrt(binomial(2n-2,n-1)); this yields P_1<=W<=B sum P_j. Conditional on one circle point, reciprocal chord factors in P_j are independent; the beta integral gives their exact Mellin transform and threshold s=1. Exponential reweighting of logarithmic chord densities yields a k=n-1 product tail asymptotic (log T)^{k-1}/(pi^k(k-1)!T). The union bound transfers the sharp order, but NOT an exact leading constant, to W, yielding E[R^s]<infinity iff s<1/2 and E[min(W,T)] asymp (log T)^{n-1}. Independently checked the n=2 identity W=2/|z1-z2| and tail 2/(pi T). Fixed n only.
